findings.title: Scheduling branches have no deterministic coverage
findings.why_it_matters: The extracted scheduler now selects interval, cron, or one-shot execution and passes distinct job options, but the suite only tests interval formatting/parsing; the Run-based provider tests require configured external providers and do not assert scheduler registration or startup. A regression that drops immediate interval execution, changes cron registration, or stops surfacing job-creation errors could pass. Add deterministic tests for each branch and the registration error path, without blocking on a real signal.
findings.evidence: internal/backup.go:500: `switch {` selects interval, cron, and default one-shot execution at lines 501-518. Existing `TestGetBackupInterval` and `TestFormatIntervalDuration` exercise only parsing/formatting; no test references `scheduleBackups` or `runScheduledJob`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add deterministic scheduler tests that verify interval and cron job registration/options, the one-shot branch, and NewJob error propagation; avoid waiting on real signals.

findings.title: Provider collection has no deterministic orchestration test
findings.why_it_matters: The newly extracted collector decides whether Bitbucket credentials are complete and iterates the token-backed provider list to invoke backups. Existing provider integration tests are conditional on external credentials, while the mock GitHub test calls the provider directly, so the orchestration and credential gates are not deterministically asserted. A provider omitted from the list or an altered gate could leave configured backups silently unrun while these tests pass.
findings.evidence: internal/backup.go:101: `if bitbucketAPITokenDefined() || bitbucketOAuthDefined() {` gates Bitbucket collection; lines 105-119 define the token provider list and invoke backups. `internal/github_mock_test.go:119` exercises GitHubHost.Backup directly, and no test references `collectProviderBackupResults`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add deterministic coverage for complete and partial Bitbucket credential pairs and for the provider selection performed by the collector, using controlled provider calls or a small injectable runner.

findings.title: Centralized notification title classifications are untested
findings.why_it_matters: All three notification transports now depend on this new helper for the success, mixed-result, and failure titles, but there are no notification tests. The existing inline switches had no direct coverage either; after centralization, a small table test would protect the shared user-visible contract and make sure each status maps to the intended title.
findings.evidence: internal/notify.go:31: `func backupStatusTitle(succeeded, failed int) string {` contains the three classifications at lines 33-38. No `notify_test.go` exists and no test references `backupStatusTitle`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a table-driven test for success, mixed success/failure, and failure counts, asserting the exact title strings.
